subject.title: feat: let plugin tools yield turns

question: Should OpenClaw make result-level yield control a permanent Plugin SDK contract, with every `executionMode: "sequential"` tool kept directly model-visible to preserve that capability?
rationale: The implementation is coherent, but it expands the public SDK and changes the meaning of an existing tool declaration across Tool Search and Code Mode; code review cannot choose that long-term compatibility boundary.

options.title: Adopt the proposed contract
options.body: Accept `AgentToolResult.control`, `yieldToolResult(...)`, and direct visibility for all sequential tools as the supported long-term plugin behavior.

options.title: Add an explicit yield capability
options.body: Keep sequential scheduling independent and add a static `mayYield`-style declaration so only yield-capable tools bypass hidden catalogs.

options.title: Defer the SDK surface
options.body: Keep plugin-owned asynchronous interactions unsupported until the broader structured-interaction direction defines a shared primitive.

recommendation.title: Adopt the proposed contract
recommendation.body: Accept `AgentToolResult.control`, `yieldToolResult(...)`, and direct visibility for all sequential tools as the supported long-term plugin behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They reviewed and merged the existing clean-yield lifecycle and previously made the key runtime-boundary decision for this behavior.
